Name: Effortless CLI
Description: Rulebook for the effortless CLI (a.k.a. ssotme / aicapture / aic): every command-line option, the request-handling state machine, the REST wire contract with transpiler tools, every config file and endpoint, the legacy-to-rebuild move map, the full test plan, and the refactor steps. Authored from the legacy source at commit a8f0f320f4417c58fa931cc4bc8164f79cbbbd97 (tag legacy-final) on 2026-08-30. This file is the single source of truth for the clean REST-only rebuild on branch effortless-cli.

Dispositions.Description: The fate of every legacy artifact, option, file, dependency and endpoint in the REST-only rebuild. Every other table with a Disposition column points here. Rows whose NeedsUserConfirmation is true are the open decisions the owner must confirm (or flip) before Step 2 begins; the recommended default is encoded in the row.

CliOptions.Description: Every command-line option the legacy CLI declares (Plossum CommandLineOption attributes), with its verbatim help text, bareword verb forms (FixParameters), how it is handled, and its fate. This table is the source of truth for the generated options class, the generated CLI reference, the -help output, and test coverage (CountOfTestCases).

schema.name: CliOptionId
schema.Description: The C# property name of the option (also the primary flag without the dash).

schema.name: Flag
schema.Description: Primary flag as typed by the user.

schema.name: Aliases
schema.Description: Comma-separated Plossum aliases (verbatim from the designer file; empty when none).

schema.name: BarewordForms
schema.Description: Comma-separated bare verbs accepted as the FIRST positional argument (from FixParameters; matched case-insensitively after ToLower). Empty when none.

schema.name: HelpText
schema.Description: Verbatim Description shown by -help. MUST be preserved character-for-character for retained options.

schema.name: IsCommand
schema.Description: True when the option selects an action (a verb); false when it modifies another action.

schema.name: ConsumesNextArgAsTool
schema.Description: True when the bareword form takes the next positional argument as the tool/value (FixParameters sets transpiler = args[1] for every matched verb; for setUrl/viewUrl/removeUrl the value is also copied into the option).

schema.name: LegacyRefCount
schema.Description: Number of "this.<option>" references in the legacy handler/project/payload code (0 means declared but never read).

schema.name: HandlerNotes
schema.Description: Where and how the option is consumed in the legacy code.

schema.name: DispositionReason
schema.Description: Why it gets this disposition; for keep-modified, the exact change.

schema.name: Name
schema.Description: Display alias for the row; mirrors Flag.

schema.name: IsRetained
schema.Description: Whether the option survives into the new build.

schema.name: NeedsUserConfirmation
schema.Description: Whether the owner must confirm this disposition.

schema.name: CountOfTestCases
schema.Description: Number of planned test cases whose primary subject is this option.

schema.name: IsTested
schema.Description: True when at least one test case targets this option.

schema.name: IsRetainedButUntested
schema.Description: Coverage gap flag: retained options with no test are not allowed to reach Step 2.

schema.name: Tier
schema.Description: primary (day-one verb), secondary (real but occasional), modifier (only meaningful with a parent command), or plumbing (for scripts/CI/tooling).

schema.name: ParentOption
schema.Description: For a modifier: the CliOptionId of the command it modifies.

schema.name: VerbFamily
schema.Description: build, clean, or describe for verb-family members sharing the downstream/Local/All/WithSubprojects pattern; null otherwise.

schema.name: Scope
schema.Description: downstream, local, all, or withSubprojects: which of the four verb-family scopes this row is, when VerbFamily is set.

schema.name: Rationale
schema.Description: The owner's why-this-exists for the option, drawn from DispositionReason/HandlerNotes and the step-09 decision table.

schema.name: HelpSummary
schema.Description: One line, at most 72 characters, shown in the default -help listing.

schema.Description: Shown by -help <option> and in the generated cli-reference.md; the full explanation, aliases, and quirks.

schema.name: Example
schema.Description: One realistic invocation of the option.

data.HelpText: Show help about how to use the Effortless CLI
data.HandlerNotes: ParseCommand: prints parser.UsageInfo header + "Syntax: effortless [account/]transpiler [Options]" + options; SuppressTranspile.
data.DispositionReason: Step 09: -help becomes grouped by category/tier and filterable (-help <category|option>, -help all) instead of one flat list of every option; behavior implemented in a later phase.
data.Description: Print usage.
data.Rationale: Every CLI needs a self-describing entry point; this is where the option taxonomy (tiers, categories, families) actually gets surfaced to a user.
data.HelpSummary: Show usage and available commands
data.HelpDetail: Prints primary-tier commands grouped by category. `-help <category|option>` narrows to one topic; `-help all` prints the flat list of every option regardless of tier.

data.HelpText: Initialize the current folder as the root of an Effortless project. An Optional parameter of force will create a sub-project.
data.HandlerNotes: ParseCommand: projectName defaults to cwd name; force = (args.Length==2 && args[1]=="force"); AICaptureProject.Init(force, name); then continueToLoad=true and build=true (init implies a build).
data.DispositionReason: Modified only in that "force" must work through the npm shim too (argv passthrough); output identical.
data.Description: Create effortless.json, .gitignore, effortless.env and an empty rulebook in cwd.
data.Rationale: The first command any new project runs; creates the effortless.json/rulebook scaffold a build needs to exist at all.
data.HelpSummary: Create effortless.json and an empty rulebook here
data.HelpDetail: Initializes the current folder as an Effortless project root. Pass `force` as the next argument to create a nested sub-project instead of failing when a parent project already exists.

data.HelpText: Saves the current command into the Effortless Project file
data.HandlerNotes: Runs the tool first (StartTranspile/SaveFileSet) then Install() in the finally block; URL tools install without running; ShouldAutoBuildForInstall builds first when -i file is missing; ProjectTranspiler ctor captures Environment.CommandLine and strips exe/verb prefixes.
data.Description: Register a transpiler step in effortless.json (and run it once).
data.Rationale: How a transpiler step becomes part of the project rather than a one-off run; every build depends on steps registered this way.
data.HelpSummary: Register a transpiler step in effortless.json
data.HelpDetail: Runs the named tool once and, on success, saves it as a step in effortless.json so future builds include it. Combine with -transpilerGroup to tag the step into a group.

data.HelpText: Removes the current command from the Effortless Project file
data.HandlerNotes: TranspileProject: name from RemainingArguments[0]; SSoTmeProject.Uninstall matches by short/qualified name + cwd RelativePath + optional -tg; prompts y/n to clean when a .zfs exists.
data.Description: Remove a registered step.
data.Rationale: The inverse of install; needed whenever a project's pipeline changes.
data.HelpSummary: Remove a registered step from effortless.json
data.HelpDetail: Removes the named step from the current folder's effortless.json entries, matching by tool name and (optionally) -transpilerGroup. Offers to clean the step's previous output first.

data.HelpText: Build any transpilers in the current folder (or children).
data.HandlerNotes: TranspileProject: BuildErrorLog.Begin("build"); project.Rebuild(cwd, includeDisabled, tg, buildOnTrigger, copilotConnect, buildLocal=false, debug, continueOnError); Finish.
data.Description: Run every enabled step at or below cwd.
data.Rationale: The core day-one verb: runs every enabled step at or below the current folder. The build/clean pair and their All/Local/WithSubprojects scopes are the whole project-pipeline family (D12).
data.HelpSummary: Build steps in this folder and its children
data.HelpDetail: Runs every enabled transpiler step registered at or below the current folder (downstream scope). Use -buildLocal for exactly this folder, -buildAll for the whole project, or -buildWithSubprojects to also include nested effortless projects.

data.HelpText: Builds all transpilers in the project
data.HandlerNotes: RebuildAll from RootPath (isBuildAll=true). D6/D12: nested effortless.json subprojects are NOT traversed; that moved to buildWithSubprojects, which passes withSubprojects=true and drives NestedProjectFinder + ChildProcessRunner.
data.DispositionReason: D6/D12 behavior change: All now means strictly "as if run from the project root". v1's buildAll also spawned "effortless -buildLocal" in every nested effortless project; the owner confirmed nested projects are generally NOT included in a build, so that traversal moved to the new buildWithSubprojects scope. Sub-project builds still spawn the current executable by path instead of "effortless" from PATH. Note the bareword "pullAll" is case-sensitive in legacy (switch lowercases input, so "pullall" never matches) - preserved as-is.
data.Description: Run every step in the whole project, excluding nested effortless projects.
data.Rationale: D6/D12: runs the project as if invoked from its root, without walking into nested effortless.json subprojects (which are normally excluded and require -buildWithSubprojects).
data.HelpSummary: Build the whole project from its root
data.HelpDetail: Builds every step in the project as if run from the project root, regardless of the current folder. Nested effortless.json subprojects are excluded (spawned separately via -buildLocal in each); use -buildWithSubprojects to include them.

data.HelpText: Build only the transpilers installed in the current folder
data.HandlerNotes: IsAtPath(exactMatch:true); also skips the parent-root-seed check.
data.Description: Run only steps whose RelativePath equals cwd.
data.Rationale: The exact-folder scope of the build family (D12); used when you only want to run what is registered right here, ignoring child folders.
data.HelpSummary: Build only steps registered exactly here
data.HelpDetail: Runs only the steps whose RelativePath equals the current folder exactly, ignoring child folders and skipping the parent-root-seed check.

data.HelpText: Builds whenever a trigger is invoked (see readme for URL)
data.HandlerNotes: TriggerBuildWatcher polls the live Airtable bridge every 3s and rebuilds after 10 quiet seconds. HTTP, status, or JSON failures stop the watcher with non-zero status; there is no silent polling fallback.
data.DispositionReason: Owner decision D2: keep the lightweight cloud-trigger monitor independently of effortless-rulebook-editor.
data.Description: Watch an Airtable base and rebuild on change.
data.Rationale: D24: a lightweight, dependency-free way to watch a cloud source (Airtable today) for changes without running a whole editor/Docker stack. Kept as its own small polling loop precisely because that is not overkill for common single-purpose use cases.
data.HelpSummary: Rebuild automatically when a remote trigger fires
data.HelpDetail: Polls the Airtable change-trigger bridge for the given base id every few seconds and rebuilds after a quiet period once it reports a change. Independent of the effortless-rulebook-editor's own change detection. Polling, HTTP, or payload failures are fatal, not a silently-ignored 'unchanged' result.

data.DispositionReason: Experimental Baserow/Copilot bridge with a hardcoded tenant id; not built today.
data.Description: Poll the copilot bridge for actions.

data.Description: Print project summary for steps at or below cwd (v2: downstream, like build; was local-only in v1).

data.HelpSummary: Describe steps in this folder and its children

data.HandlerNotes: LoadInputFiles/ImportFile: comma split, "newname=pattern" rename, trailing "?" marks optional, directory part validated against project scope (parent project allowed), glob via DirectoryInfo.GetFiles(pattern); binary detected by control chars; contents zipped.
data.Description: Input file(s) sent to the tool.
data.Rationale: The explicit way to send specific files to a tool instead of relying on its own fileset discovery; used by scripted/CI invocations and by -execute-adjacent local tooling.
data.HelpSummary: Send specific input file(s) to the tool
data.HelpDetail: Comma-separated file names or glob patterns sent to the tool. Supports `newname=pattern` renaming and a trailing `?` to mark a file optional.

data.HelpText: Output filename
data.HandlerNotes: Copied into payload.CLIOutput by SaveCLIOptions (LegacyRefCount counts only "this.output"; it IS used).
data.Description: Requested output filename for the tool.
data.Rationale: D21: output shape is the tool's call, not the CLI's — a tool may write one file or a whole tree. The CLI's only job is to pass the requested name through.
data.HelpSummary: Requested output name, passed through to the tool
data.HelpDetail: Whatever the tool decides: the CLI passes this value to the tool as OutputFileName and does not interpret, validate, or default it. The tool may use it as a single file name or as the root of a directory tree it writes.

data.HelpText: Clean all transpilers installed in and downstream of this folder
data.HandlerNotes: Three branches: with a .zfs given via -i (clean that ledger); with no remaining args (project.Clean(cwd, preserveZFS, purge, debug) + reverse seed replacements); with a tool name (result.CleanFileSet instead of SaveFileSet after running).
data.Description: Delete generated files recorded in .zfs ledgers.
data.Rationale: The build/clean pair is the core loop; clean removes what a previous build wrote so the next build starts from a known state.
data.HelpSummary: Delete generated output here and below
data.HelpDetail: Deletes files recorded in the .zfs ledger for every step registered at or below the current folder. Combine with -purge to also clean orphaned ledgers for steps no longer registered, or -preserveZFS to keep the ledger files themselves.

data.HelpText: Clean all project transpilers
data.HandlerNotes: CleanRunner.CleanAll from RootPath (cleanAll=true). D6/D12: nested effortless.json subprojects are NOT traversed; that moved to cleanWithSubprojects, which passes withSubprojects=true.
data.DispositionReason: D6/D12 behavior change: All now means strictly "as if run from the project root". v1's cleanAll also spawned "effortless -clean" in every nested effortless project; that traversal moved to the new cleanWithSubprojects scope.
data.Description: Clean the whole project, excluding nested effortless projects.
data.Rationale: D12: the whole-project scope of clean, mirroring buildAll; also removes empty folders left behind.
data.HelpSummary: Clean the whole project from its root
data.HelpDetail: Cleans every step's output across the whole project (spawning -clean in nested effortless.json subprojects) and removes folders left empty afterward.

data.HelpText: Cleans only transpilers installed in the current folder
data.HandlerNotes: IsAtPath(exactMatch:true).
data.Description: Clean only steps registered exactly at cwd.
data.Rationale: D12: the exact-folder scope of clean, mirroring buildLocal.
data.HelpSummary: Clean only steps registered exactly here
data.HelpDetail: Cleans only the steps whose RelativePath equals the current folder exactly.

data.HelpText: When supplied with clean, runs clean on all orphaned transpilers
data.HandlerNotes: RemoveUnusedZFSFiles: any .zfs under .ssotme not matching a current step is cleaned (in its RelativePath) then deleted, plus its debug .xml. Only when !preserveZFS.
data.Description: Also clean ledgers of steps that are no longer registered.
data.Rationale: Keeps a project's .ssotme ledger directory from accumulating stale entries for steps that were uninstalled without ever being cleaned.
data.HelpSummary: Also delete ledgers for steps no longer registered
data.HelpDetail: When passed with clean, any .zfs ledger under .ssotme that no longer corresponds to a currently-registered step is cleaned (its recorded output files are deleted) and then the ledger file itself is removed, along with its debug XML. Has no effect when -preserveZFS is also set.

data.HelpText: Don't clean the output before cooking
data.HandlerNotes: SaveFileSet(skipClean): skips CleanFileSet of the previous .zfs before writing.
data.Description: Write outputs without first cleaning the previous run.
data.Rationale: Lets a tool run write outputs on top of whatever is already there instead of first deleting the previous run's files; useful when a tool's own output is additive or when a previous clean already ran.
data.HelpSummary: Write outputs without cleaning the previous ones
data.HelpDetail: Skips deleting the files recorded in the previous .zfs ledger before a step writes its new output. The previous output is left in place; anything the new run does not overwrite survives untouched.

data.HelpText: The account which the transpiler belongs to
data.HandlerNotes: Also auto-extracted from "acct/tool" names when no URL resolves. D20: resolution never fails on acct/tool alone - if acct/tool does not resolve in the catalog, the CLI resolves tool and behaves as tool -account acct, failing only if tool itself does not resolve either. Sent as cliAccount.
data.DispositionReason: D20: acct/tool extraction behavior is changing from an implicit fallback to a documented never-fail contract (ToolResolutionRules R6/R7).
data.Description: Credential/account selector for a tool.

data.HelpDetail: Selects the account used for credential injection (see -setAccountAPIKey) and is also auto-extracted from an `acct/tool` name when the combined name does not resolve in the catalog (D20: resolution then falls back to `tool -account acct` instead of failing).

data.HelpText: Pin this project's step to a specific catalog version or URL
data.HandlerNotes: New in v2 (D17). Stores a hard pin (a catalog version key or a literal URL) on this project's installed step in effortless.json (PinnedVersion), distinct from the per-user -setToolUrl override which applies machine-wide across every project. IMPORTANT: ProjectToolFreshness.Apply takes clearPins; the automatic build-time gate (CommandDispatcher.EnsureProjectToolsCurrent) passes false so a deliberate pin survives a build, while -upgrade/-upgradeAll pass true and unpin. Without that split the gate would null PinnedVersion on every build and -pin could never take effect. Invocation shapes: the flag form is 'effortless <tool> -pin <version|url>'; the bareword form 'effortless pin <tool> <version|url>' is normalized by CliArgumentParser.NoDashCommandForms into the flag form (the trailing value becomes -pin's value and the tool stays in the tool position). 'pin <tool>' with no value falls through to Plossum, which reports "Missing required value for option pin".
data.DispositionReason: D17: a step is either pinned or it follows HEAD. -pin is the explicit way to fix a version or URL for this project; -upgrade (alias unpin) or -upgradeAll clear it. Default stays unpinned = HEAD; pin-on-install by default is not assumed.
data.Description: Pin an installed step to a version or URL for this project.
data.Rationale: D17: gives a project a way to freeze a step's version deliberately (reproducibility, a known-good release) without reaching for the per-user -setToolUrl override, which is not project-scoped.
data.HelpSummary: Pin an installed step to a version or URL
